dish: Smoked brisket, pulled pork, rib tips — Southern-style 'cue
w: Pullman smokehouse of Dominique Leach, 2023 'Master of 'Cue' on Food Network's BBQ Brawl — one of the city's best barbecue spots.

dish: Tacos al pastor carved off a live-fire trompo ($1 Mondays)
w: Little Village's unlikely al pastor champion — a Chinese-Thai takeout counter whose trompo makes some of the best al pastor in Chicago.

dish: Steak tacos on fresh house tortillas, rice and beans, cafeteria line
w: The 1950 tortilla maker's cafeteria on 26th Street — fresh tortillas off the line and one of Little Village's best Mexican restaurants.

dish: Cafeteria-line fried chicken, meatloaf, candied yams, peach cobbler
w: Austin's soul-food cafeteria (1997) of Mississippi-born MacArthur Alexander — a West Side institution whose regulars included Barack Obama.

dish: Dipped Italian beef with peppery jus, then homemade lemon Italian ice
w: University Village corner stand (since 1929) — the Infatuation calls its jus the best in Chicago; cash-only ice counter next door.

dish: Craft beer and cocktails at a bowling-lane bar top
w: Pilsen's Green-Restaurant-certified bar and cultural space — solar panels, salvaged fittings, a bar made from a bowling lane.

address: 6257 S Cottage Grove Ave, Chicago, IL 60637
dish: Diner breakfasts, fried chicken and soul-food plates
w: Chicago's oldest restaurant — a Woodlawn lunch counter opened in 1892 for World's Fair builders; Muhammad Ali ate here between workouts. Moved across 63rd to Woodlawn Station in 2019.

dish: Craft beer in a frozen-in-time liquor-store bar; Kimski's 'Maria's Standard' Polish sausage with soju mustard and kraut-chi
w: Bridgeport's community bar run by the Marszewski family (Maria, from Busan) — with Kimski, the Korean-Polish kitchen added in 2016.

dish: Regional Mexican plates and tortas from a Topolobampo alum, BYOB
w: Casual, affordable Pilsen BYOB from chef Alfonso Sotelo (ex-Bayless) — Michelin-listed regional Mexican cooking.

dish: Cheap beer and burgers at the University of Chicago's local since 1948
w: Hyde Park's bar of record (1948) — Saul Bellow's 'local haunt', where students, professors and neighbours have always mixed.

dish: Po'boys — fried catfish, shrimp, roast beef debris, the oyster-and-beef 'Northern Peacemaker'
w: James Beard winner Erick Williams' Louisiana tavern (2022) a block from his Virtue — live New Orleans jazz on first Wednesdays.

address: S Halsted St at the Ramova Theatre, Bridgeport, Chicago
dish: Ramova chili, duck-fat corn dogs and Other Half beer brewed on site
w: Bridgeport's 1929 Spanish-courtyard movie palace reborn in 2024 as a concert hall, with its old diner (famous for chili, closed 2012) and a brewery taproom beside it.

dish: Vegan soul food — smothered seitan steak, cornbread dressing, vegan mac and cheese
w: Chatham's vegan soul-food pioneer since 1982 (as Original Soul Vegetarian), renamed and renovated for its 40th year.

address: E 47th St at S King Dr, Bronzeville, Chicago
dish: Shrimp-and-bacon cheese grits, peach bourbon French toast, peach cobbler
w: Chef Cliff Rome's Bronzeville breakfast café — Southern brunch on 47th Street, with a visit from Barack Obama (WGN).

dish: Sizzling beef, salt-and-pepper squid and congee until 4am
w: Chinatown's Hong Kong-style café for the late-night crowd — open till 4am most nights, 24 hours on weekends.

dish: Asian-inspired cocktails (ube, mango brandy) plus Moon Palace's soup dumplings and dong po pork
w: Chinatown's first speakeasy, a moody Blade Runner-esque lounge hidden behind Moon Palace Express — the family's restaurant still serves its soup dumplings up front.

dish: Frozen custard flavour of the day and jumbo burgers
w: Milwaukee-area custard stand since 1950 — one of the city's 'big three' with Gilles and Leon's; the Greenfield store is the original HQ.

dish: Goat birria consommé, cabeza and tongue tacos
w: Pilsen birrieria with a half-dozen-item menu — Time Out: 'one visit to this one before you stop caring about the rest.'

dish: Mexican hot chocolate, espresso and focaccia sandwiches amid local art
w: One of Pilsen's first coffeehouse-galleries (1994), opened by Eleazar Delgado in an old barber shop at 18th & Bishop — a neighbourhood living room for artists.

address: Thalia Hall, S Allport St at 18th St, Pilsen, Chicago
dish: (closed) — beer-driven gastropub plates; Punch House cocktails downstairs
w: CLOSED 31 Dec 2023: the Thalia Hall gastropub that won a Michelin star (2016) and helped revive Pilsen's 1892 hall; Thalia Hall's music room carries on.
